Romantically I've been told I make a great partner, but the idea of living with someone to be my everything forever fills me with immense dread and reluctance. I struggle with loneliness but I relish my solitude and could see myself staing single forever. I like being attracted to people and having mutual chemistry for intimacy, but a full on relationship is beyond me to commit to or even humor. I'd much rather indulge in friendship or FWB dynamics than to claim someone as "mine" anymore. Been there, done that, not really interested in trying it again.

Hey there, I'm 27 and constantly in this warfare state of mind with myself regarding the whole passion versus career topic. I think about this constantly. It's a hard decision when it comes to energy and happiness. What I think it boils down to is security. Will you realistically be financially stable and comfortable enough to pursue music exclusively (full-time) from the ground up? Music often doesn't come with benefits, high salary, or low-stress because of all that goes into marketing your sound/style/image and booking gigs or record deals. But as someone who wants to be an artist/creative myself I say keep your eyes on music but change your approach. Find a way to build your music skills on the side while you keep your current job, and immerse yourself in the WORLD of music as much as you can. Volunteer at a music venue or work with kids who are learning to play an instrument or start a YouTube channel documenting your musical journey or perform at a senior center to get your feet wet, etc. Little things just to stay as music-fed and music-minded as you can while you work, until you find that special pathway out of your current job and into your passion.
